assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a new window on the universe: the IceCube detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos (2013) is a clear, original discovery that founded neutrino astronomy at energies no other messenger probes. It fits the principle that the discovery should be at the centre.
assessment.attribution: Only one credited name is supplied, so the configuration is simple. Halzen was the central figure in conceiving, driving and leading IceCube, but a discovery made by a large collaboration rests on many people (instrument builders, analysts); the supplied credit may under-represent others, and I cannot add names.
assessment.maturity: Mature: independent analyses and channels confirm the diffuse flux, the 2017 TXS 0506+056 coincidence gave a first source, and the 2023 Galactic-plane result adds more. The sources of the bulk of the flux remain mostly unidentified, but the discovery itself is secure.
uncertainties: Credit for a collaboration-scale discovery is concentrated in one name and may be disputed or incomplete.
The origin of most of the diffuse flux is still unresolved, which affects how the committee frames the citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP delivered precision full-sky maps of the cosmic microwave background and fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model (age, geometry, matter content, reionization), turning cosmology into a quantitative science. Lasting impact is very high and the results are understood and cited everywhere.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission as PI, Page led key instrument and calibration work and Spergel led the cosmological analysis, so these three are a defensible, distinct split across mission, instrument and interpretation. The WMAP science team and the earlier COBE and Planck work complicate pure attribution, but the trio is coherent.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: results were independently confirmed and refined by Planck and ground experiments, and the interpretation is stable. The risk is that recognition of CMB cosmology has already been given (COBE 2006, Peebles 2019), so novelty relative to those prizes must be argued.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier CMB and cosmology prizes may count against it.
Planck largely superseded WMAP in precision, so the committee may prefer a different framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock (magic-wavelength trapping proposed by Katori) enables fractional frequency stability and accuracy at the 10^-18 level, redefining precision measurement and opening tests of fundamental constants, relativity and dark-matter couplings. The invention is clear and the impact is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and first demonstrated Sr lattice clocks; Ye brought them to the highest accuracy and developed many-body clock physics and links to frequency combs. Both are credited names and form a natural two-person prize. Other groups (for example Lemonde, Takamoto, Lisdat) are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent clocks worldwide reach comparable performance, and a redefinition of the second is under discussion. Timing is good, although the 2005 prize (Hall, Hänsch) and the 2012 prize (Wineland) for related precision and optical techniques may be weighed.
uncertainties: Closeness to the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-trap prizes could be seen as incremental.
Possible need to include other groups if attribution is argued more broadly than the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators and their experimental realization in HgTe quantum wells is a conceptual and experimental landmark that created a field of topological materials. Importance and originality are high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive theory (Z2 classification, quantum spin Hall in graphene model), while Molenkamp led the experimental HgTe observation following Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's prediction. The omission of Zhang and Bernevig-Hughes from the supplied credit is a real allocation problem, but within the credited names the trio is the strongest.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three-dimensional topological insulators were observed by several groups, and the framework is stable and widely applied. Recognition is plausible now, though Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz (2016) already honoured topological phases.
uncertainties: Missing people (Zhang, Bernevig, Hughes) and priority questions among Kane-Mele, Bernevig-Zhang and Moore-Balents.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation addresses the horizon and flatness problems and predicts a nearly scale-invariant spectrum of primordial fluctuations that matches CMB observations; it is arguably the central idea of modern early-universe cosmology. Worthiness in originality and impact is very high.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed the scenario, Linde the new and chaotic inflation that make it workable, and Mukhanov the quantum origin of fluctuations that make it testable. Starobinsky, Sato and others (not in the supplied credit) have a strong claim, so allocation is genuinely contested and cannot be resolved with these names alone.
assessment.maturity: Partly mature: the fluctuation spectrum is well confirmed, but the key distinctive prediction, primordial gravitational waves, is unobserved, and alternatives and the multiverse/measure problems persist. As a theorist I would be cautious about recognising a paradigm before a decisive empirical signature.
uncertainties: No detection of primordial B-modes, so inflation as the mechanism is not conclusively established.
Priority disputes involving Starobinsky and others outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum computation with trapped ions and its experimental realization (gates, entanglement, algorithms) founded a leading platform for quantum information processing. Conceptual originality is high and the practical impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the 1995 proposal; Blatt led key experimental implementations, though Wineland's group (already recognised in 2012) and Monroe also made decisive experimental contributions and are not credited here. The trio is a reasonable theory-plus-experiment configuration but does not capture all experimental credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a platform, with commercial machines and independent confirmation, but the field's ultimate outcome (scalable fault-tolerant computing) is not settled, and the 2012 prize and the 2025 circuits prize already touch quantum control.
uncertainties: Overlap with Wineland's 2012 recognition and with competing platforms.
Uncertain split between theory and experiment contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar-timing evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, probably from supermassive black-hole binaries, opens a new band of the gravitational-wave spectrum and is relevant to gravity, cosmology and black-hole physics. Importance potentially high.
assessment.attribution: The result is from several collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA, IPTA), and the supplied names represent regional leaders and pulsar-timing pioneers rather than clearly decisive individuals; the fair prize configuration is hard to draw. Individual credit would be contentious.
assessment.maturity: Premature in my view: the 2023 evidence is at about the 3 to 4 sigma level, the specific Hellings-Downs correlation is only suggestive, and the astrophysical source (versus new physics) is unresolved. Confirmation by independent datasets and higher significance is awaited.
uncertainties: Significance and origin of the signal remain unconfirmed.
Collaboration credit is diffuse and the named individuals may not be the decisive contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states launched the field of moire quantum materials, with a very large following and clear originality.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery of the correlated and superconducting states. Cao and others made the key experimental measurements and are not credited, so the experimental credit may be incomplete. The theory-plus-experiment pairing is otherwise clear.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: reproduced by many groups, but the nature of the superconductivity and correlated states is still debated and the field is under ten years old, so a prize may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity is not settled.
Possible premature recognition and incomplete experimental credit.
